source.title: On the Omnipresence of Spurious Local Minima in Certain Neural Network Training Problems

record.tranche_reason: Proves theoretically that broad classes of fixed neural network architectures have spurious local minima, but does not run gradient training or test the listed benchmark, width-comparison, initialization, learning-rate, or normalization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's theorems establish spurious local minima under stated assumptions. Its CIFAR-10 training example and gradient-based failures are cited from prior work, not results of this study; no numerical training experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study proves existence of spurious local minima for fixed fully connected architectures. It does not establish how often standard gradient training reaches them or whether extra student neurons reduce that frequency in V2's teacher-student setting. Its other results likewise do not test V1–V6. Remark 5.5 explicitly omits numerical training tests and attributes the discussed experiments to prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the stated assumptions, the networks possess continua of spurious local minima, with spuriousness established through a consequence of universal approximation. The authors also establish ill-posedness of best approximation for networks whose images are not dense in the specified spaces. These conclusions do not establish failure frequencies under standard initialization.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical loss-landscape results; no gradient-training recipe or empirical benchmark run.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Theorem 3.1's assumptions, spurious local minima attain the best affine approximation loss and form a set of Hausdorff dimension at least m − d − 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed fully connected networks with continuous nonpolynomial activations having nonconstant affine segments and hidden widths at least two possess continua of spurious local minima for nonaffine targets under the stated loss assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Theorem 3.2's assumptions, spurious local minima attain the best constant approximation loss and form a set of Hausdorff dimension at least m − 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed fully connected networks with continuous nonpolynomial activations and a constant segment in at least one hidden layer possess continua of spurious local minima for nonconstant targets under the stated loss assumptions.

record.problems: The results are conditional mathematical theorems, not empirical evidence about how often gradient training reaches these minima or whether practical benchmark recipes stall. The paper explicitly omits numerical tests of the constructed bad initializations.
record.rows_left_out: No other own result rows bear on the listed versions. CIFAR-10 and gradient-based failure experiments mentioned in Remark 5.5 are explicitly attributed to prior work and omitted.

untested.parts: Training classification error of randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and recipe or size comparisons.
Gradient descent outcomes from standard initialization in realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, their frequency across widths, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special initialization, or Fixup.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature trajectories, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Existence of spurious minima at arbitrary widths does not contradict V2's claim about how frequently gradient descent reaches them. Constructed bad starting points and the informal extension to residual architectures do not test V4 or V3.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train convolutional networks from random initialization or measure classification error, including on CIFAR benchmarks or corrupted labels.
Does not use a teacher-student setup, compare spurious-minimum frequency as widths grow, or test extra student neurons.
Does not compare plain and residual networks across depth or test normalization and initialization recipes.
Does not compare initializations or measure training speed or trainable depth.
Does not test learning rates, loss trajectories, curvature, or stability thresholds.
Does not compare batch normalization with alternatives or measure training speed.

rows.subject: Fully connected feedforward neural networks with nonconstant affine activation segments (theorem class)
rows.size_stated: Depth L; hidden widths wi ≥ 2; parameter-space dimension m; input dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes existence of a continuum of spurious local minima for the training objective under its assumptions.

conditions.value: continuous, nonpolynomial, affine and nonconstant on an open interval in each hidden layer
Gâteaux differentiable in its first argument with nonzero partial derivative away from the target; affine best approximation exists

rows.measure: Existence of a set of spurious local minima with Hausdorff dimension at least m − d − 1; each has the loss of the best affine approximation.
rows.value: A set E with dimH(E) ≥ m − d − 1 consists of spurious local minima.
rows.note: Analytical theorem, not a measured training run; applies to the stated class and assumptions.
rows.check: Theorem 3.1 and its dimension bound are correctly recorded, but this is an analytical existence result, not a measurement of training behavior. It cannot determine any listed version's effect; 'observed' applies only to the separate existence claim.

rows.subject: Fully connected feedforward neural networks with a constant activation segment (theorem class)
rows.size_stated: Depth L; widths wi; parameter-space dimension m; input dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes existence of a continuum of spurious local minima for the training objective under its assumptions.

conditions.value: continuous, nonpolynomial, with a constant segment in one hidden layer
Gâteaux differentiable in its first argument with nonzero partial derivative away from the target; constant best approximation exists

rows.measure: Existence of a set of spurious local minima with Hausdorff dimension at least m − 1; each has the loss of the best constant approximation.
rows.value: A set E with dimH(E) ≥ m − 1 consists of spurious local minima.
rows.note: Analytical theorem, not a measured training run; the theorem does not require a minimum hidden width beyond the stated architecture.
